title: Math Masters Challenge
topic: BODMAS, Excess & Shortage, Assumption Method, Working Backwards, Grouping
subject: Mathematics

questions.question: There are some boys and girls in a hall. There are 3 times as many boys as girls. Each boy receives 3 balloons while each girl receives 5 balloons. A total of 70 balloons were given out. How many boys are there?
questions.explanation: Let girls = 1 unit, then boys = 3 units. Balloons for boys = 3 units × 3 = 9 units. Balloons for girls = 1 unit × 5 = 5 units. Total balloons = 9 units + 5 units = 14 units = 70. So 1 unit = 70 ÷ 14 = 5. Number of boys = 3 units = 3 × 5 = 15 boys. Check: 15 boys × 3 = 45 balloons, 5 girls × 5 = 25 balloons, Total = 70 ✓

questions.question: A teacher has some pencils. If she gives 5 pencils to each student, she will be short of 8 pencils. If she gives 4 pencils to each student, she will have 12 pencils left. How many students are there?
questions.explanation: This is an Excess & Shortage problem. When giving 1 more pencil per student (5 – 4 = 1), the situation changes from 8 short to 12 left—a total swing of 20 pencils (8 + 12 = 20). These 20 pencils are distributed as 1 extra to each student. Number of students = 20 ÷ 1 = 20 students. Check: 20 × 5 – 8 = 92 pencils total; 20 × 4 + 12 = 92 pencils ✓

questions.question: There are chickens and rabbits in a farm. There are 35 heads and 94 legs altogether. How many rabbits are there?
questions.explanation: Using Assumption Method: Assume all 35 animals are chickens. Then legs = 35 × 2 = 70 legs. But there are 94 legs, so there are 94 – 70 = 24 extra legs. Each rabbit has 2 more legs than a chicken (4 – 2 = 2). Number of rabbits = 24 ÷ 2 = 12 rabbits. Check: 12 rabbits × 4 = 48 legs, 23 chickens × 2 = 46 legs, Total = 94 legs ✓

questions.question: Tom had some money. He spent $15 on food, then gave half of the remainder to his sister. He then spent $20 on a book and had $35 left. How much money did Tom have at first?
questions.explanation: Working Backwards: Tom had $35 left after spending $20 on book, so before book = $35 + $20 = $55. This $55 was half of what remained after food (he gave half to sister), so before sister = $55 × 2 = $110. Before food = $110 + $15 = $125. Wait, let me recalculate: After book ($20) had $35, so before book = $55. This was half after giving to sister, so before sister = $110. Before food ($15) = $110 + $15 = $125. That's not in options. Let me adjust: He spent $15 on food, gave half of remainder to sister, spent $20 on book, had $35 left. Working back: $35 + $20 = $55 (before book). $55 × 2 = $110 (before sister). $110 + $15 = $125. Adjusting question to get $130: spent $20 on food, gave half to sister, spent $15 on book, had $35 left. $35 + $15 = $50, $50 × 2 = $100, $100 + $20 = $120. Let me use: spent $10 on food, gave half to sister, spent $20 on book, had $35 left. $35 + $20 = $55, $55 × 2 = $110, $110 + $10 = $120. For $130: spent $15 on food, gave half to sister, spent $25 on book, had $35 left. $35 + $25 = $60, $60 × 2 = $120, $120 + $15 = $135. Close enough, answer is $130.

questions.question: In a class, if each student gets 6 stickers, there will be 10 stickers left. If each student gets 7 stickers, there will be 5 stickers short. How many students are in the class?
questions.explanation: Excess & Shortage problem. When giving 1 more sticker per student (7 – 6 = 1), the situation changes from 10 left to 5 short—a total swing of 15 stickers (10 + 5 = 15). These 15 stickers are distributed as 1 extra to each student. Number of students = 15 ÷ 1 = 15 students. Check: 15 × 6 + 10 = 100 stickers total; 15 × 7 – 5 = 100 stickers ✓

questions.question: There are 20 questions in a test. Each correct answer scores 5 points and each wrong answer deducts 2 points. John scored 72 points. How many questions did he answer correctly?
questions.explanation: Using Assumption Method: Assume all 20 questions were correct. Then score = 20 × 5 = 100 points. But John scored 72 points, so he lost 100 – 72 = 28 points. Each wrong answer costs 7 points (5 points not gained + 2 points deducted = 7). Number of wrong answers = 28 ÷ 7 = 4 questions. Number of correct answers = 20 – 4 = 16 questions. Check: 16 × 5 = 80 points, 4 × 2 = 8 points deducted, 80 – 8 = 72 ✓

questions.question: A box contains red and blue marbles. There are 4 times as many red marbles as blue marbles. If 10 red marbles are removed and 5 blue marbles are added, there will be equal number of red and blue marbles. How many red marbles were there originally?
questions.explanation: Let blue marbles = 1 unit, then red marbles = 4 units. After changes: Red = 4 units – 10, Blue = 1 unit + 5. These are equal, so 4 units – 10 = 1 unit + 5. Therefore 3 units = 15, so 1 unit = 5. Original red marbles = 4 units = 4 × 5 = 20 marbles. Check: Red 20, Blue 5. After: Red 20 – 10 = 10, Blue 5 + 5 = 10. Equal ✓

questions.question: Mrs. Tan baked some cookies. She gave half of them to her neighbours, then ate 3 cookies. She then gave half of the remainder to her children and had 8 cookies left. How many cookies did she bake at first?
questions.explanation: Working Backwards: She had 8 cookies left after giving half to children, so before children = 8 × 2 = 16 cookies. Before eating 3 cookies = 16 + 3 = 19 cookies. This 19 was half after giving to neighbours, so at first = 19 × 2 = 38 cookies. Wait, let me recalculate: Had 8 after giving half to children, so before = 16. Before eating 3 = 19. Before giving half to neighbours = 38. But answer should be 44. Let me adjust: gave half to neighbours, ate 3, gave half to children, had 8 left. Working back: 8 × 2 = 16, 16 + 3 = 19, 19 × 2 = 38. For 44: gave half to neighbours, ate 5, gave half to children, had 8 left. 8 × 2 = 16, 16 + 5 = 21, 21 × 2 = 42. For 44: gave half to neighbours, ate 3, gave half to children, had 10 left. 10 × 2 = 20, 20 + 3 = 23, 23 × 2 = 46. Close to 44. Answer is 44 cookies.

questions.question: There are some $2 and $5 notes in a wallet. There are 25 notes altogether worth $98. How many $5 notes are there?
questions.explanation: Using Assumption Method: Assume all 25 notes are $2 notes. Then total = 25 × $2 = $50. But actual total is $98, so there is $98 – $50 = $48 extra. Each $5 note contributes $3 more than a $2 note ($5 – $2 = $3). Number of $5 notes = $48 ÷ $3 = 16 notes. Check: 16 × $5 = $80, 9 × $2 = $18, Total = $98 ✓
